title: Online shop — order to delivery
subtitle: How an order moves through storefront, payments, stock, warehouse, carriers, returns and finance
source: Illustrative example for the blog post *Understanding Is the New Bottleneck*. A composite of a typical mid-size online retailer, not a real client.
summary: A customer checks out in the **shop**. Payment is captured, a fraud check runs, and the order waits until the **nightly sync** sends it to the **warehouse system (WMS)**. The warehouse plans picking in waves, picks and packs, and hands parcels to the **carrier**. Finance books revenue at dispatch. Returns come back through a portal and are refunded after inspection.

summary.title: The one idea to keep
summary.text: Two things run on last night's data: the orders the warehouse sees, and the stock the shop shows. Same-day dispatch fails on the first; most back-orders come from the second.

legend.label: Confirmed
legend.description: Stated by the business or seen in the systems

sections.title: Storefront and checkout
sections.summary: The shop sells against its own copy of stock.
blocks: The catalogue lists SKUs with prices and promotions. At checkout the shop checks **available stock**, captures payment with the payment provider, and saves the order as **Placed**.

blocks.text: Available stock is last night's WMS figure minus orders placed since. Returns, damages and manual adjustments in the warehouse today are invisible to the shop until tonight.

sections.title: Payments and fraud
sections.summary: Payment is captured at checkout; risky orders are held for review.
blocks: The payment provider captures the full amount at checkout. A fraud score above the threshold puts the order **On hold** for manual review; held orders are skipped by the nightly sync.

blocks.text: Who reviews held orders at weekends is not defined. See [[questions:fraud_weekend]].

sections.title: The nightly sync
sections.summary: Once a night, at 02:00, in both directions.
blocks: At 02:00 the integration sends every Placed order to the WMS and copies WMS stock levels back to the shop.
Everything downstream inherits this delay: wave planning, picking, carrier booking and the stock the shop sells against.

sections.title: Warehouse: waves, picking, packing
sections.summary: Orders are picked in waves, checked per SKU.
blocks: The WMS groups received orders into waves. Pickers collect each SKU; packing checks every line.
If any SKU is missing, the **whole order** becomes a back-order. The shop does not split orders.

blocks.text: Whether partial shipments should be allowed is undecided. See [[questions:partial]].

sections.title: Carriers and dispatch
blocks: Packed orders get a carrier label from the carrier API. The carrier collects once a day at 16:00. Dispatch triggers the customer email and the revenue entry in the ERP.

sections.title: Returns and refunds
sections.summary: Refund after inspection, not on receipt.
blocks: Customers start a return in the portal. When the parcel arrives, the warehouse inspects it: sellable items go back to stock, damaged ones are written off. The refund is issued after inspection.

blocks.text: Restocked items reach the shop's available stock only after the next nightly sync.

sections.title: Finance
sections.summary: The ERP books revenue at dispatch and reverses it on refund.
blocks: The ERP records revenue when an order ships and a credit note when a refund is issued. Back-orders are cash received but not yet revenue.

sections.title: Target: same-day dispatch
sections.summary: Orders placed before 14:00 should leave the same day.
blocks: The business wants same-day dispatch for orders placed before 14:00.

blocks.text: That needs orders in the WMS within minutes (a **real-time order feed**), live stock in the shop, and a carrier collection late enough to take the 14:00 orders.

walkthroughs.title: Follow one order: Maya's T-shirt and jeans
walkthroughs.intro: An example case; the rules come from the process above. On Tuesday at 13:40, Maya buys a blue T-shirt in size M and a pair of jeans in size 32. The shop shows one pair of jeans left.

steps.title: Maya checks out
blocks: The shop checks its available stock, the payment provider captures the full amount, and the fraud score is low.

steps.title: When does the warehouse see it?
blocks: She ordered at 13:40, before the 14:00 cut-off the business wants.

choices.label: Within minutes, so it can leave today

steps.title: Not today
blocks: Today orders only travel in the nightly sync. The 14:00 cut-off is the *target*, not how it works now.

steps.title: The nightly sync sends it
blocks: At 02:00 the order reaches the WMS, about twelve hours after she paid. The same sync overwrites the shop's stock copy.

steps.title: Were the jeans really there?
blocks: The shop showed one pair left when Maya paid.

choices.label: Yes: the shop checked stock at checkout
Not necessarily: the shop checked last night's copy

steps.title: The shop's figure was a copy
blocks: Available stock is last night's WMS figure minus today's orders. A pair damaged in the warehouse that morning was still on sale.

steps.title: Wednesday's first wave
blocks: The T-shirt is on the shelf. The jeans are not: the last pair was damaged on Tuesday morning.

choices.label: The whole order becomes a back-order
The T-shirt ships; the jeans follow later

steps.title: No partial shipments
blocks: The shop doesn't split orders today. One missing SKU holds the whole order. Whether to allow splits is still [[questions:partial|open]].

steps.title: Back-ordered
blocks: Maya gets a back-order email. She has paid for both items, finance has no revenue yet, and nothing has shipped. Same-day dispatch would need a [[map:sync|real-time feed]] *and* live stock.

questions.title: Should partial shipments be allowed?
blocks: Faster for customers, but more parcels, carrier costs and several revenue entries per order. See the what-if on the map.

questions.title: Are back-orders part of the same-day promise?
blocks: If yes, partial shipments become almost unavoidable.

questions.title: Who reviews held orders at weekends?
blocks: Held orders skip the sync, so a Friday-evening hold can wait until Monday night.

questions.title: Can the WMS publish stock changes in real time?
blocks: Without it, same-day dispatch still sells stock that is gone.

questions.title: Will the carrier add a later collection?
blocks: A 16:00 collection leaves two hours to pick and pack 14:00 orders.

choices: Orders only reach the warehouse in the nightly sync
explain: The warehouse can't pick an order it hasn't received. The sync, not picking speed, sets the delay.

quiz.q: Blue L is out of stock. Maya orders blue M. What happens?
explain: Stock is checked per **SKU**, not per product. Blue M is its own SKU.

quiz.q: The shop showed one pair of jeans in stock at checkout. Is it guaranteed to ship?
choices: No, the shop checked last night's copy of stock
explain: **Available stock** is the last sync's figure minus today's orders. Today's damages and adjustments are invisible until tonight.

quiz.q: One item in a three-item order is missing. What happens today?
choices: The two items ship, the third follows
The whole order becomes a back-order
The missing item is cancelled automatically
explain: The shop doesn't split orders. Partial shipments are an open question.

quiz.q: Finance talks about a *sale*, the warehouse about a *shipment*. What are they?
choices: The same Order under different names
explain: Same thing, three names. Pick one term (**Order**) and use it everywhere.

quiz.q: When is the refund for a return issued?
choices: When the customer starts the return
explain: Inspection decides restock or write-off; the refund follows it.

quiz.q: A return is restocked at 11:00. When can the shop sell it again?
explain: The shop sells against its copy of stock, refreshed at 02:00.

quiz.answer: A batch of received orders the warehouse picks together.

quiz.q: Same-day dispatch needs which two data changes?
quiz.answer: A real-time order feed to the WMS, and live stock in the shop.

quiz.q: An order goes On hold for fraud review on Friday evening and is released on Saturday. When does the warehouse see it?
choices: At the next 02:00 sync after release
explain: Held orders skip the sync; a released order travels in the next one.
